decision.summary: Priya reported a once-a-minute chirp on a 2019 sealed-battery CO alarm past its 7-year life; call dropped. Treated as probable end-of-life alarm (urgent, not a confirmed CO emergency), logged JOB-101 and separate routine fan job JOB-102, texted safety advice, and asked the landlord to approve replacement.

answers.question: Is this a carbon monoxide emergency, a battery issue, or an end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely an end-of-life alarm: single chirp about once a minute since last night (not continuous), sealed battery (so not a replaceable battery), fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life so expired April 2026. Not treated as a confirmed CO emergency (no continuous alarm, no symptoms reported, boiler serviced 2025-11), but handled as urgent and the tenant was given leave-and-call-0800 111 999 advice if it changes. Cannot be fully confirmed remotely.

answers.question: Who is responsible for fixing it, citing the tenancy clause where relevant?
answers.answer: The landlord, via the agency. Clause 12.8 (tenant replaces batteries) doesn't fit because the battery is sealed and the unit has expired, so the whole alarm must be replaced. Clause 12.9 means the tenant reported promptly as required. Clause 12.17 (tenant pays avoidable call-outs) does not apply: the fault is not avoidable by the tenant and it was not an out-of-hours emergency call-out.

answers.question: What actions did you take, and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent JOB-101 (CO alarm) and routine JOB-102 (extractor fan); requested landlord approval up to £300 (APR-104); set follow-up for 12 Oct. Texted the tenant: do not remove the battery, it is likely end of life, urgent job logged with a 72h target, safety advice and 0800 111 999/999 if continuous alarm or symptoms, fan logged separately, next update by 12 Oct.

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't take the battery out: it's a sealed unit fitted in 2019 and a chirp like this usually means it has reached the end of its life, so it needs replacing, not a new battery. We've logged an urgent job (JOB-101) and are asking your landlord to approve a replacement; our target is within 72 hours. If the alarm ever sounds continuously, or you or anyone feels headachy, dizzy or sick, leave the flat, call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if in immediate danger) and tell us. Please don't use the boiler if you smell gas. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan separately (JOB-102, routine). We'll update you by Monday 12 October.
